plan:
# Working session · 2026-11-02 · Download button, adire lane

## Pitch

**Flight deck designer:** Resist Export. A file panel where you mask files out of a download before it is packed. Hand masks on single files. Rule masks on groups. A preview of the bundle as it will land. One download button that tells the truth from idle to done. Then a receipt that notices when your masks drift from what you downloaded. The person who opens the zip next week is the one I'm speaking for. They need to know what's missing and why.

**Cartographic designer:** Offline Area. Download map tiles for a field trip. You paint a resist over regions you don't need, the bundle shrinks, the button reports tile counts. Components: area mask canvas, zoom-level picker, size estimate, download button, tile receipt, storage meter. It breaks out of the list frame. Shrink it to 320 and it still has to read.

**Ergonomist:** Report Pull. One monthly report PDF. A prepare step with honest named stages, a cached copy that serves the repeat instantly, a retry on failure. Six rows: format picker, date range, prepare status, download button, cached-copy note, history. No percentages anywhere. A bar that says 63% with no real job behind it is a lie.

**Tidal library custodian:** Archive Shelf. A reading room of deposited folders. Detail rises and falls as you pass each shelf, and the shelf label never moves. You choose what to take, and the take is packed. Components: shelf strip, tide detail, take list, pack button, slip receipt, return log. It has to be beautiful. Show me the packed state before you call it packed.

## Clash

**Ergonomist:** Report Pull is the plainest answer to the brief. Prepare, complete, repeat. Nothing else to argue about.

**Flight deck designer:** It's the third loader in a week. 10-28 had load stages and 10-29 had an import stage track. The repeat action is the only new part. In Resist Export the repeat has to decide: same bundle, or the masks changed.

**Tidal library custodian:** That decision is a claim. Show it. If "Download again" reuses a cached bundle, the label has to say "same bundle" and the receipt has to carry its id.

**Cartographic designer:** Good. Area painting is drag-only, so I'll drop Offline Area. I'll keep the smallest-size check. At 320 px a two-pane file panel collapses, and the button can't end up under the fold.

**Ergonomist:** Then the button's pending state counts files the packing loop has really packed. "Preparing · 7 of 21". And I need the exact moment it stops: the label swaps once on completion and holds. No pulse after that.

**Flight deck designer:** Rule masks and hand masks should look different on the quiet rows. A dashed edge for a rule, a solid bar for a hand mask, with the word beside each. That way the accent stays for the selected row.

**Tidal library custodian:** The preview gets my method. "Show resisted" brings masked rows back into view, dimmed and struck. The count label above stays fixed.

**Cartographic designer:** That's better than the shelf pitch. Making the reveal reversible gives it a job. I'd add one thing: the receipt should restore the downloaded mask set. That makes resist reversible end to end.

## Decision

The team builds Resist Export, a file panel where a visitor masks files and groups out of a bundle, downloads it with honest preparation feedback, and repeats or restores it knowing exactly which files the download holds.

Concept: Resist Export

**Contributions.** The Flight deck designer set the direction and the quiet-row rule: dashed edge for rule masks, solid bar for hand masks, the accent kept for selection. The Cartographic designer set the panel frame and the 320 px check, and proposed restoring masks from the receipt. The Ergonomist set the counted pending state, the dedupe on presses and the single settle point. The Tidal library custodian set the fixed-label reveal and the rule that "same bundle" is shown by an id.

**Rejected direction.** Report Pull. It was clear and useful, but its prepare-and-retry shape repeats 10-28 load stages and 10-29 import stage track. Its repeat action had no decision to make.

**Adire reading.** Resist dyeing appears as interaction only. Masks protect files from the bundle the way resist protects cloth from the dye. Rules mask groups, and removing a rule lifts only its own layer. The preview reveals what was resisted. No motifs, no imagery and no claims of authenticity. Reference: https://www.vam.ac.uk/articles/cloth-of-a-continent-africa-fashion.

**Source.** No component_source was supplied. The idea-bank note for the riffle label button shaped row 4 in three ways: a native button, a reserved label width and no housing decoration. No source code is used.

**Why six.** Each row answers a separate question:
1. Which files are in.
2. Which groups are out.
3. What will arrive.
4. Does the panel hold at 320 px.
5. Do it.
6. Does the download still match.

Dropping any row leaves one of those questions unanswered. A seventh row would be a mask-preset picker, and it would duplicate row 2.

## Build notes

1. Compute `included` in one pure function from handMasks, rules and exceptions. Rows 1, 3, 5 and 6 read only that function. Hash the sorted ids with a 4-character FNV-1a for the bundle id, so "same bundle" is checkable.
2. Reserve the row 5 label width by rendering every label variant in a hidden grid cell stack, so the widest label sets the width. Set `min-height: 44px` on the button, the rule toggles, the tree rows and the disclosure.
3. Test at 320px container width with long names such as `layouts/cover-v1-client-revision-final.indd`. Names must wrap, the foot must stay pinned, and the preview label must not move when Show resisted toggles. Report this as a manual check, not as verified.

components.input: Click or tap Preview bundle at narrow widths. Keyboard: Tab to it, Enter or Space toggles.
components.outcome: The panel shows two panes at 480px and above. Below that it shows one column with the preview behind a disclosure.
components.recovery: Widening the container restores two panes and keeps the disclosure state for the next narrow view.
components.mechanism: CSS container query on the panel. The body scrolls between a sticky header and a sticky foot. The foot holds row 5 at a minimum height of 44px and full width when narrow. Long file names wrap and are never truncated.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-11-01 details side panel managed focus in a dialog. This frame manages space and keeps the action reachable without a dialog.
components.usefulness: A download button that scrolls away on a phone stops the task.
components.creativeDifference: The narrow layout trades the preview pane for a disclosure, and the button stays fixed in the foot.
states: wide: two panes, reached at container width 480px and above
narrow: one column with a Preview bundle disclosure
preview-open: disclosure expanded, aria-expanded=true
320px: 16px padding and a full-width foot button
focus: 2px ring on the disclosure

components.name: Download bundle button
components.description: Native button that prepares, completes and repeats a download, counting real packed files and reusing a cached bundle when the masks match.
components.purpose: Prepare and save the bundle, and make the repeat action say whether it is the same bundle.
components.use: A designer downloads, unmasks one font, and the button reads 'Prepare new bundle · 1 change'.
components.input: Click or tap the button, minimum 44px tall. Keyboard: Tab to it, Enter or Space. Escape stops a preparation in progress.
components.outcome: The label moves from 'Download 17 files · 33.8 MB' to 'Preparing · 7 of 17' to 'Downloaded'. It then holds at 'Download again · same bundle'.
components.recovery: Presses while preparing are ignored. Escape stops the preparation and returns the label to idle with 'Stopped at 7 of 17'. A demo failure reads 'Not prepared · Retry'.
components.mechanism: A packing loop over the included files, 60ms per file, increments the shown count. No percentage is shown. The result is a local JSON manifest Blob saved through an object URL and an anchor with a download attribute. The bundle id is a short hash of the sorted included ids. A repeat with a matching id reuses the cached Blob. Label width is reserved for the longest label.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-30 copy link button reported version-aware repeats. This adds counted preparation and a cached file for the repeat.
components.usefulness: This button is the core task.
components.creativeDifference: The repeat label states whether the masks changed before the press.
states: idle: count and size, reached on load
pressed: 1px sink on pointer or key down
preparing: disabled with 'Preparing · n of N'
complete: 'Downloaded' for 1.2s, then settled
repeat-same: 'Download again · same bundle'
repeat-changed: 'Prepare new bundle · n changes'
stopped: via Escape
failed: 'Not prepared · Retry'
empty: disabled, reached when the bundle is empty
focus: 2px ring
reduced-motion: label swaps without transition

components.name: Bundle drift receipt
components.description: Status receipt naming the downloaded bundle, which flags drift when masks change and can restore the downloaded mask set.
components.purpose: Record what was downloaded and say when the screen no longer matches it.
components.use: A designer reads 'Bundle a3f9 out of date · 1 file added since' and presses Restore masks.
components.input: Click or tap Show changes or Restore masks. Keyboard: Tab to each, Enter or Space.
components.outcome: The receipt reads 'spring-catalogue · 17 files · 33.8 MB · 14:06 · bundle a3f9'. On drift it lists the added and removed files.
components.recovery: Restore masks sets hand masks, rules and exceptions back to the a3f9 snapshot. An Undo restore option is offered for 5s.
components.mechanism: role=status, with polite announcements on completion and on the first drift only. The mask snapshot is stored with the bundle id. Drift is a set difference between the snapshot include set and the current include set.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-30 link options field flagged clipboard drift. This receipt also restores the earlier masks.
components.usefulness: It shows which files the downloaded copy holds after the button has reset.
components.creativeDifference: The mask can be reapplied exactly from the record.
states: hidden: before the first download
current: receipt line
drifted: 'out of date' with change counts
changes-shown: list of added and removed files
restored: 'Masks restored to a3f9' with Undo
focus: 2px ring

demo.sharedState: One store holds the 23 spring-catalogue files with tags and sizes, handMasks, active rules, exceptions and the last bundle {id, snapshot, blob, time}. Rows 1 and 2 write masks. Row 3 reads the computed include set. Row 4 frames all rows. Row 5 packs the include set and writes the bundle. Row 6 compares the bundle snapshot with the current set and can write the snapshot back.
